turns.text:
`flow.py` streams the ten-line text constant line by line, splits each line into lowercase punctuation-free words on a two-worker farm, counts them on a keyed three-worker farm (so every occurrence of a word lands on the same counter), then a single ranking node merges the partial totals and emits the ten most common pairs for the printing sink.

Run it with `python flow.py`; it prints the top ten words right-aligned with their counts (ties broken alphabetically). `build(source=...)` accepts any iterable of lines, so you can test it with `tq.from_iterable` and a sample instead of the built-in `TEXT`.
